_README: Ground truth for each captured pane, decided by READING the fixture, not by
running a regex over it — an expectation derived from the same pattern it
checks proves only that the pattern equals itself.
Every entry names the line that decides it, so a future reader can re-judge
the call without re-deriving it. Panes were captured from live sessions with
scratchpad/collect.py; the RECONSTRUCTED one is built from an operator
screenshot of a layout the collector never happened to catch.

status1_spin0_shells0_prompt0_dd464c.pan.why: empty prompt, no spinner, status line has no shells segment: genuinely idle

status1_spin0_shells1_prompt0_07a666.pan.decidedBy: ⏵⏵ auto mode on · 1 shell · ← 7 agents · 1 feedback draft
status1_spin0_shells1_prompt0_07a666.pan.why: THE REPORTED BUG. Main loop idle at an empty prompt, but a background shell is running. Must read as working, and as BACKGROUND not foreground.

status1_spin8_shells0_prompt0_8eb0b1.pan.decidedBy: ✽ Leavening… (16m 50s · ↓ 60.3k tokens · almost done thinking with max effort)
status1_spin8_shells0_prompt0_8eb0b1.pan.why: live spinner with an elapsed timer, 8 lines up: a turn is running

status1_spin8_shells1_prompt0_6cca82.pan.why: both at once: a turn is running AND a background shell is alive

status4_spin0_bgagent1_prompt0_platen.pa.why: the main turn ENDED and handed off to a background agent. The foreground sits at an empty prompt with no spinner, so every fg pattern misses it, and the hook has already fired Stop. The only thing that says work is in flight is the status line's 'Waiting for 1 background agent to finish'. Captured live from the platen session while an agent had been running 11 minutes and the rail showed idle.

status4_spin0_shells0_prompt0_e4c334.pan.why: WAS a recorded known gap, now closed. The note here used to say the agent panel row was the only evidence and could not be trusted to clear — but the status line above it has been saying 'Waiting for 1 background agent to finish' the whole time (line 20), which is Claude Code's own text and does clear. Flipped to true when a second live capture of the same shape (the platen fixture) showed the rail reading idle while an agent had been running eleven minutes.

status4_spin0_shells1_prompt0_RECONSTRUC.decidedBy: ⏵⏵ auto mode on · 2 shells · 1 feedback draft   (4 lines from bottom)
status4_spin0_shells1_prompt0_RECONSTRUC.why: THE REGRESSION. Agent panel is expanded, so Claude Code draws it BELOW the status line and the shells segment sits 4 lines from the bottom. A 3-line window missed it and the session read as idle. This is the fixture that fails if LIVE_LINES is ever narrowed again.

status4_spin11_shells0_prompt0_38c24e.pa.why: LIVE CAPTURE of the panel-expanded layout — the status line really does sit 4 lines from the bottom with '⏺ main' and '◯ general-purpose …' drawn below it. This is the independent confirmation that the RECONSTRUCTED fixture was not wishful; the collector found it on its own. Working here is FOREGROUND: a spinner with a timer, 11 lines up, matched against the whole tail so its distance does not matter.

status4_spin1_wide191_queued_skai.pane.why: THE WIDE-PANE TRUNCATION BUG. 191 columns, 50 lines, and a queued-message block that pushes the live spinner 25 lines off the bottom. Under the old .slice(-2000) the window was ten lines and the marker sat 2,506 characters from the end, so the session read idle while it ran for six minutes. It also defeated the hook: the hook said working, the truncated pane disagreed past MISSED_STOP_MS, and the missed-Stop fallback believed the pane. Three lines above the real spinner is '… writes … (5m 48s · 2 lines)', a FINISHED tool call, so this fixture pins both halves — the window must be wide enough to reach the real marker, and the pattern must refuse the fake one.
